_note: 1838 Mob Attack Statistics -- Self-Defense & Resistance evidence table, from Michiko's live Google Sheet 'Copy of Self-Defense' (1838 Research folder, doc 1FPHdouFNGO5eNuJT7B6dC371uLn2idPaQEx3MXodFe8), pulled 2026-08-14. Main source page: https://www.1838blackmetropolis.com/attackstats . Each entry keeps the sheet's row text; 'names' lists the individually-named Black defenders/complainants (plus the named white ally Thomas Shipley) to be linked to people records. Rows describing unnamed or collective defenders have an empty names list and load as data only. Prisoners-for-Trial IMG_#### citations link to the page photographs in the project Drive (resolved 2026-08-14 per Michiko's QA).

entries.category: Collective Armed Defense from a Building
entries.description: When the Killers/'Rats' attacked and returned in greater numbers, shots were fired from the Boyer House Tavern. 'Firearms, as well as bricks, were freely used by both parties, the whites being the principal sufferers.'
entries.outcome: White men shot: Redman Prendible (10-17 slugs in back), a man named 'Black'/'Scott' (head & breast), + others; ~17 injured, whites principal sufferers. (# = documented gunshot min.)
entries.defenders: Samuel Williams (owner) and Black men inside

sources.t: Public Ledger, Aug 20, 1849; The Baltimore Sun, Aug 21, 1849

entries.category: Collective Armed Defense from a Building
entries.description: California House residents mounted a full defense with guns; the tavern was saved from destruction in August. Firearms were later taken from the tavern by police.
entries.outcome: Tavern defended and saved (August); foreshadows the October attack

sources.t: Public Ledger, Aug 21, 1849; The Baltimore Sun, Aug 21, 1849

entries.category: Collective Armed Defense from a Building
entries.description: From a window of the one-story meeting-house/school-room (likely Temperance Hall's Sabbath schoolroom) a Black man discharged a loaded gun at the crowd.
entries.means: Loaded gun; also an old sword
entries.outcome: Did no damage; mob wrested away the gun and an old sword and took him prisoner, beating him bloody on the way.

entries.category: Collective Armed Defense from a Building
entries.description: A three-story house on St. Mary's became a garrison of about 60 Black people armed with pistols and makeshift weapons. When the mob heard of it they moved north into the City and met police resistance; officials had the men leave two at a time.
entries.outcome: Standoff; occupants extracted in pairs. NOTE: 1849 source recounts officials 'found mostly terrified refugees' — the garrison framing is contested.

sources.t: Hazard's Register

entries.category: Collective Armed Defense from a Building
entries.description: Black residents had prepared defenses; when the mob reached Ninth & Christian it met gunfire from the houses. Five discharges in all. Defenders escaped out the back before the mob forced entry.
entries.outcome: A musket ball passed through one mobber's body; another had his kneecap shot off (taken to hospital). Defenders escaped intact.

sources.t: United States Gazette, Jul 18, 1835; Hazard's Register v.16

entries.description: Met the mob with gunfire from a house; the shots struck three white men. Van Brackle was found with a brass pistol 'heavily loaded and capped.' Accounts differ on details (2-4 defenders; who reached the roof).
entries.outcome: Three white men shot (Public Ledger names Patrick Monahan, Benjamin Raymon/Bieman, John White). Defenders dragged out and beaten near to death; Van Brackle survived under Officer Yerkes's protection.
entries.defenders: Henry Van Brackle (teenager ~15), Anthony Harvey, and a third Black man

entries.description: 'An elderly woman, who possessed considerable acuteness and observation, gave me a very clear account of what passed in her own dwelling, where I saw her. The door and the windows were forced in; and she hid herself in a closet, whence she heard and saw all that took place. Some money, that she had left on the chimney-piece, was the first thing seized. The furniture was then destroyed; while several men in black masks, and disguised with shabby coats and aprons, searched about the room to see if any one lay there concealed. She recognised one man's voice, reproving a lad with an oath, for saying they had done enough. This man she washed for. The next day he told her he should not employ her any longer. She laid her complaint before the mayor; and the party accused was bound over to appear at the proper time. While in court, she saw a well dressed man step up to the mayor, and whisper something in his ear. The colored people were immediately ordered out of court.'

sources.t: Edwin Abdy
